problem:
Consider the matrices

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}],\,C=[\begin{aligned}0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- $AB=BA={I}_{3}$
- $BC=CB={I}_{3}$
- $A={B}^{-1}$
worked_solution:
- First, we check whether $AB=BA={I}_{3}.$ Computing $AB$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}∗ & -1 & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗ \\ ∗ & ∗ & ∗\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne {I}_{3}.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

So, statement I is false. As a result, $A\ne {B}^{-1}$ and statement III is false too.

- Now, we check whether $BC=CB={I}_{3}.$ Computing $BC$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}BC & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Likewise, computing $CB$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}CB & =[\begin{aligned}0 & -\frac{1}{2} & -1 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{2} & 0 \\ 1 & \frac{1}{2} & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 \\ -1 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={I}_{3}.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

So, statement II is true.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only".
